bucket: Smart Controls, Demand Flexibility & Thermal Storage

census.bucket: Smart Controls, Demand Flexibility & Thermal Storage (Buildings)

variations.name: Smart thermostats and home energy management systems (HEMS)
variations.description: Connected thermostats and whole-home energy platforms learn occupancy and price signals to trim and shift HVAC load (the largest controllable home load), forming the entry point for residential demand flexibility.

companies.name: Google Nest
companies.what: Market-defining learning thermostats; tens of millions deployed, with the Nest Renew grid service spun out into VPP operator Renew Home.
companies.signal: 4th-gen Learning Thermostat launched 2024; Nest fleet anchors a planned 1 GW Texas VPP

companies.name: ecobee
companies.what: Smart thermostat pioneer with eco+ optimization and deep utility DR program integrations.
companies.signal: Acquired by Generac for up to $770M (closed Dec 2021); now Generac's grid-services front end

companies.name: Mysa
companies.what: Smart thermostats for high-voltage electric baseboard/in-floor heat and mini-splits — loads conventional thermostats can't control.
companies.signal: $11M continued funding Oct 2024 (~$43M total); fleet manages 700+ MW of HVAC load in North American VPPs

companies.name: tado°
companies.what: European leader in smart heating control (TRVs + thermostats) with dynamic-tariff load shifting after acquiring aWATTar.
companies.signal: 5.5M+ thermostats connected; reached operating profitability after strong 2025 (IPO/SPAC plans previously shelved)

companies.name: Sensibo
companies.what: Israeli maker of retrofit IR controllers that make ductless mini-splits and window ACs smart and DR-ready.
companies.signal: Global DTC + utility channel; category leader in retrofit AC control

companies.name: Resideo (Honeywell Home)
companies.what: Licenses the Honeywell Home thermostat brand at mass-market scale and is consolidating smart-home distribution.
companies.signal: NYSE: REZI; acquired Snap One for ~$1.4B (2024)

companies.name: Savant
companies.what: Luxury whole-home orchestration (HVAC, lighting, power) tying comfort control to backup power and load management.
companies.signal: Acquired GE Lighting (2020) to extend into energy/power products

companies.name: Schneider Electric
companies.what: Schneider Home / Wiser HEMS bundles inverter, battery, smart panel, EV charging and thermostat control in one residential ecosystem.
companies.signal: Global electrical incumbent; Schneider Home launched 2023 across US channels

variations.name: Smart electrical panels and circuit-level control
variations.description: Replacing or augmenting the breaker panel with metered, switchable circuits lets homes shed and shift loads automatically, stretch battery backup, and electrify without service upgrades.

companies.name: SPAN
companies.what: Flagship smart panel with per-circuit metering/control; pivoting toward utility-scale deployments as a grid-edge flexibility asset.
companies.signal: Raising ~$176M Series C (early 2026) on top of >$200M prior; Landis+Gyr distribution partnership (2024)

companies.name: Lumin
companies.what: Retrofit responsive-load panel that adds circuit control beside the existing breaker box instead of replacing it.
companies.signal: Acquired by ABB (Jan 2025) after Sunnova partnership and ABB minority investment in 2023

companies.name: Savant Power
companies.what: Breaker-level power modules and storage built on the GE Lighting acquisition, sold through the custom-install channel.
companies.signal: Part of Savant's energy push since 2020 GE Lighting deal

companies.name: Eaton
companies.what: AbleEdge smart breakers and home energy management integrating EV charging and backup within standard load centers.
companies.signal: Major electrical OEM embedding circuit control in mainstream distribution

companies.name: Schneider Electric (Square D)
companies.what: Square D Energy Center combines panel, backup interface and energy management in one enclosure.
companies.signal: Pushing smart-panel functions into the high-volume Square D installer base

companies.name: Leviton
companies.what: Smart load centers with app-controllable, metered smart breakers at near-conventional price points.
companies.signal: 2nd-gen smart load center in wide retail/electrician distribution

variations.name: Meter collars and panel-upgrade-avoidance hardware
variations.description: Devices that tap power at the meter socket or share existing 240V circuits let homes add solar, batteries, EV charging and heat pumps without a costly panel/service upgrade — removing a key electrification bottleneck.

companies.name: ConnectDER
companies.what: The leading meter socket adapter (collar) for interconnecting solar/storage/EV charging at the meter; new IslandDER adds whole-home backup islanding.
companies.signal: $35M Series D (Dec 2024, Decarbonization Partners/BlackRock-Temasek); 25,000+ adapters deployed, approved in 20+ states

companies.name: Siemens
companies.what: Invested in and partnered with ConnectDER to commercialize a UL-certified meter-mounted EV charging adapter through its eMobility business.
companies.signal: Incumbent channel validation for the meter-collar form factor

companies.name: NeoCharge
companies.what: UL-certified Smart Splitter that shares an existing 240V dryer/range outlet between an appliance and an EV with app-based scheduling.
companies.signal: $329 consumer product; utility rebate partnerships (e.g., SMUD $200 rebate); saves $1,500-$4,800 vs rewiring

companies.name: simpleSwitch
companies.what: UL-certified EV energy management switch that load-shares a 240V circuit between a primary appliance and an EV charger or heat pump, no WiFi required.
companies.signal: Shipping products ($699 240EV); positioned around NEC load-calc workarounds

companies.name: Splitvolt
companies.what: Plug-and-play splitter switches (NEMA 10-30/14-50) for dual loads on one 240V circuit, cETLus certified.
companies.signal: Consumer retail traction in EV-charging accessories

variations.white_space: Sparse by design: meter-socket devices need utility-by-utility approval and UL certification, a multi-year moat that has left ConnectDER nearly alone in the collar form factor. With ~50M US homes on 100A service and panel upgrades costing $2,500-$10,000, low-cost meter-level interconnection and load management is a large, underserved opening as heat pump/EV adoption collides with service limits.

variations.name: Residential demand response and VPP aggregation platforms
variations.description: Software (and increasingly battery-led offerings) that aggregate thermostats, water heaters, batteries and EVs into dispatchable virtual power plants, paying households to shift load and selling capacity to utilities and markets.

companies.name: Renew Home
companies.what: Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners-backed merger of Google Nest Renew and OhmConnect; the largest US residential thermostat-based VPP operator.
companies.signal: ~3 GW under management; building a ~1 GW Texas VPP with NRG and Google Cloud by 2035

companies.name: EnergyHub
companies.what: Utility-facing DERMS/VPP platform (Mercury) orchestrating thermostats, EVs, batteries and water heaters for dozens of utility programs.
companies.signal: Alarm.com-owned; one of the largest US residential flexibility networks with millions of enrolled devices

companies.name: Virtual Peaker
companies.what: Cloud DERMS focused on making device-agnostic residential DR programs easy for small and mid-size utilities/co-ops.
companies.signal: $16.6M Series A (Moore Strategic Ventures) plus new round led by Veriten (Aug 2025); ~$31M total

companies.name: Leap
companies.what: API-based wholesale market access that lets any device OEM or aggregator monetize flexibility without becoming a market participant itself.
companies.signal: $33.5M Series B + $12M (2023); 13x growth in load under management over two years

companies.name: Uplight
companies.what: Utility customer-engagement platform that added grid orchestration by buying AutoGrid, creating an end-to-end VPP stack for utilities.
companies.signal: Manages ~8,300 MW of flexible resources post-AutoGrid acquisition (closed 2024)

companies.name: AutoGrid
companies.what: Pioneering VPP/DERMS software spanning residential through C&I, formerly owned by Schneider Electric.
companies.signal: Sold by Schneider Electric to Uplight (announced Dec 2023, closed 2024)

companies.name: Swell Energy
companies.what: Solar+storage VPP developer running programs for Hawaiian Electric and SMUD.
companies.signal: Insolvent early 2025 — liquidating via assignment for benefit of creditors after layoffs; HECO Battery Rewards program halted

companies.name: Tesla
companies.what: Runs Powerwall-based VPPs (with PG&E, in Texas via Tesla Electric, and others) using its Autobidder/fleet software.
companies.signal: Paid Powerwall owners $9.9M through VPPs in 2024; CA Powerwall fleets delivered ~500 MW in July 2025

companies.name: Base Power
companies.what: Texas retail electricity provider that installs its own home batteries for a monthly fee and operates them as a VPP — vertically integrated flexibility.
companies.signal: $1B Series C (Oct 2025) led by Addition at $4B valuation; expanding beyond Texas with domestic battery manufacturing

companies.name: sonnen
companies.what: German home-battery maker whose sonnenVPP runs battery-only VPP programs, including a Texas program with Solrite.
companies.signal: Shell-owned; launched battery-only Texas VPP programme (2025)

variations.name: Commercial AI building management and HVAC optimization
variations.description: Cloud/AI layers (or full autonomous control platforms) sit on top of building HVAC to predict loads and continuously retune equipment, typically cutting HVAC energy 10-25% with little capital outlay.

companies.name: BrainBox AI
companies.what: Deep-learning autonomous HVAC control retrofitted onto existing BMS across ~14,000 buildings; cuts HVAC energy up to 25%.
companies.signal: Acquired by Trane Technologies (closed Jan 3, 2025); now Trane's 'BrainBox AI Lab'

companies.name: 75F
companies.what: Vertically integrated wireless sensors, controllers and cloud AI offering full BAS replacement for mid-size commercial buildings at a fraction of legacy cost.
companies.signal: Additional $45M Series B (Feb 2025) incl. Carrier Ventures; earlier backing from Siemens/Next47 and Breakthrough Energy

companies.name: PassiveLogic
companies.what: Physics-based digital-twin 'generative autonomy' platform (Hive) aiming to replace conventional building controls entirely.
companies.signal: $74M Series C (Sept 2025); >$125M total from NVIDIA's NVentures, Johnson Controls, Brookfield, Prologis

companies.name: Runwise
companies.what: Heat computers + wireless sensors that optimize steam/hydronic boilers in older multifamily/CRE stock — a niche legacy BMS ignores.
companies.signal: $55M Series B (June 2025, Menlo Ventures); 10,000+ buildings, >$100M customer savings to date

companies.name: Parity
companies.what: Remote 24/7 HVAC optimization-as-a-service for multifamily and hotels, guaranteeing utility savings and stacking demand-response revenue.
companies.signal: $19M Series B (June 2024, Idealist Capital); ~100M sq ft under management; CA expansion 2025

companies.name: GridPoint
companies.what: Energy management + controls + DR for small-format commercial chains (restaurants, retail, banks), a segment too small for BAS integrators.
companies.signal: $45M strategic round (Mar 2025, Marunouchi/Mitsubishi) for Japan/Korea expansion; 20,000+ buildings; earlier $150M HASI facility

companies.name: Phaidra
companies.what: Reinforcement-learning 'virtual plant operator' (Alfred) for mission-critical cooling — data centers and industrial facilities — cutting cooling energy ~25%.
companies.signal: $50M+ Series B (Oct 2025, Collaborative Fund; NVIDIA, Index participating); $92.5M total

companies.name: BuildingIQ
companies.what: ASX-listed pioneer of predictive HVAC optimization (heritage of today's AI-BMS category).
companies.signal: Subsidiaries in receivership (2021); Australian entity in creditors' voluntary liquidation (2022) — cautionary tale on services-heavy economics

companies.name: Honeywell
companies.what: Forge/Advanced Control for Buildings brings closed-loop AI optimization to its massive installed BMS base.
companies.signal: Global BMS incumbent embedding autonomous optimization

companies.name: Johnson Controls
companies.what: OpenBlue digital platform layers AI optimization and net-zero services over Metasys installed base; also invests in startups (PassiveLogic).
companies.signal: Strategic investor in PassiveLogic's 2025 Series C

variations.name: Fault detection & diagnostics, submetering and energy analytics
variations.description: Continuous analytics on equipment and circuit data find faults, waste and savings opportunities that manual audits miss, turning energy data into persistent efficiency — though pure monitoring has struggled to capture value on its own.

companies.name: Clockworks Analytics
companies.what: Category-defining automated fault detection & diagnostics (FDD) used by large healthcare, university and corporate portfolios.
companies.signal: 20+ year FDD track record (KGS Buildings heritage); profitable niche leader

companies.name: SkyFoundry
companies.what: SkySpark analytics engine embedded by hundreds of OEMs/integrators; progenitor of the Project Haystack data-tagging standard.
companies.signal: Company-claimed >1B sq ft under analysis globally

companies.name: Verdigris
companies.what: High-frequency AI circuit-level submetering hardware, increasingly targeting data-center power monitoring.
companies.signal: Venture-backed; pivoted upmarket to critical facilities

companies.name: Sense
companies.what: ML load disaggregation that identifies individual appliances from one sensor; now embedding its software directly into utility smart meters (Landis+Gyr et al.).
companies.signal: $195M raised; exiting direct-to-consumer hardware Dec 31, 2025 to go utility software-only — emblematic D2C retreat

companies.name: Emporia
companies.what: Low-cost Vue circuit monitors, EV chargers and batteries forming a budget home energy management ecosystem.
companies.signal: High-volume consumer traction in energy monitoring and EVSE

companies.name: Copper Labs
companies.what: Wireless meter-edge devices that give utilities real-time, appliance-level insight from existing gas/water/electric meters without AMI upgrades.
companies.signal: Utility pilots/deployments across US; venture-backed

companies.name: Facilio
companies.what: Property operations + connected-buildings platform unifying FDD, maintenance and energy across portfolios.
companies.signal: $35M Series B (Dragoneer, 2022); global CRE customers

companies.name: Carbon Lighthouse
companies.what: Efficiency-as-a-service pioneer using sensor-driven analytics (CLUES) to guarantee NOI gains for CRE.
companies.signal: Shrank to single-digit headcount by end-2024 and relaunched as 'Centinel' — evidence that audit-style analytics struggled to scale

variations.white_space: Standalone monitoring keeps getting commoditized: consumer disaggregation is being absorbed into smart meters (Sense's pivot) and CRE analytics into BMS/FDD suites (Carbon Lighthouse's contraction). The open ground is analytics that closes the loop — automatically actuating controls or monetizing flexibility — rather than producing reports.

variations.name: C&I demand response and flexibility market access
variations.description: Aggregators enroll factories, big-box retail and campuses to curtail or shift load for capacity and energy market payments — the cheapest firm 'capacity' on the grid and a mature, consolidating market.

companies.name: Voltus
companies.what: Software-only C&I DER/DR aggregator across all nine US/Canadian wholesale markets; pioneered 'bring-your-own-capacity' deals (first customer: Google, up to 100 MW in PJM).
companies.signal: 8.1 GW flexible capacity managed in 2025; $240M paid to customers in record 2025

companies.name: CPower
companies.what: National pure-play C&I demand-side energy manager monetizing curtailment, generation and storage across US markets.
companies.signal: LS Power-owned; >6 GW of flexible capacity across thousands of C&I sites

companies.name: Enel X (Enel North America)
companies.what: Inheritor of EnerNOC, one of the world's largest C&I DR portfolios; kept DR as a core focus while divesting its distributed-energy-solutions unit to Calibrant (2024).
companies.signal: 2025-27 plan reaffirms US/Canada DR growth; global DR leader

companies.name: GridBeyond
companies.what: Irish AI-driven flexibility platform co-optimizing C&I load, onsite generation and batteries across UK, Ireland, US, Japan and Australia.
companies.signal: ~€52M Series C (2023); multi-market expansion

companies.name: Blueprint Power
companies.what: Turned NYC commercial buildings into market-participating power plants by aggregating onsite DERs and selling flexibility to the grid.
companies.signal: Acquired by bp (2021) into bp Launchpad; building-to-grid model absorbed by an oil major

variations.name: Behind-the-meter thermal energy storage (ice and phase-change)
variations.description: Freezing water or melting phase-change materials off-peak stores cheap/clean energy as heat or cold, shifting HVAC and refrigeration — roughly half of building peak load — without batteries' cost, fire risk or degradation.

companies.name: Trane Technologies (CALMAC)
companies.what: CALMAC ice-storage tanks are the legacy standard for shifting commercial cooling to off-peak hours, integrated with Trane chillers.
companies.signal: Thousands of installations worldwide over 40+ years; mature niche product line

companies.name: Nostromo Energy
companies.what: IceBrick modular cell-based ice storage retrofittable to commercial chiller plants, operated as a dispatchable VPP asset.
companies.signal: $305.5M DOE LPO conditional loan commitment (Dec 2024) for up to 193 California buildings (~170 MW/450 MWh); first wholesale-market TES participation with Olivine (Nov 2025)

companies.name: Ice Energy
companies.what: Ice Bear rooftop ice batteries for small commercial AC, sold via utility contracts (SCE).
companies.signal: Filed Chapter 7 in Dec 2019 despite 25.6 MW of SCE contracts; assets continued by Thule Energy Storage — the sector's defining failure

companies.name: Sunamp
companies.what: Compact phase-change 'Thermino' heat batteries replacing hot-water cylinders, charging from off-peak tariffs, solar PV or heat pumps.
companies.signal: UK government-backed £9.25M EXTEND LDES demonstration; Midea heat-pump compatibility launch (Mar 2025)

companies.name: Phase Change Solutions
companies.what: Plant-based BioPCM mats tuned to specific temperatures for passive load shifting in buildings, telecom shelters and cold chain.
companies.signal: Deployed across dozens of countries; partnership-driven model

companies.name: Viking Cold Solutions
companies.what: PCM thermal storage inside frozen-food warehouses that rides through peaks and cuts refrigeration energy up to 35%.
companies.signal: Installations across US, LatAm, Europe, Asia; claims LCOE below 2 cents/kWh

companies.name: Steffes
companies.what: Grid-interactive electric thermal storage (ETS) room and central furnaces that bank cheap off-peak electricity as heat, long used by co-ops.
companies.signal: Decades of utility-program deployments across northern US/Canada

companies.name: Axiom Cloud
companies.what: Software that turns existing supermarket refrigeration into a thermal battery for demand shifting and fault detection, no new hardware.
companies.signal: Deployed with major US grocers; venture-backed

companies.name: Harvest Thermal
companies.what: Smart pod that runs a CO2 heat pump to charge a hot-water tank off-peak, serving both space heating and hot water from stored heat.
companies.signal: Early-stage; California pilot deployments

variations.white_space: Thermal storage is cheap physics with hard economics: Ice Energy went Chapter 7 even holding utility contracts because project sales were slow and margins thin, and incumbents treat ice as a niche chiller accessory. The opening is financeable, VPP-grade TES with stacked revenues — exactly what Nostromo's DOE-backed, 193-building aggregation model and Axiom's software-only approach are testing — plus heat batteries riding heat-pump electrification in space-constrained homes.

variations.name: Grid-interactive water heating (CTA-2045/EcoPort thermal batteries)
variations.description: Electric and heat-pump water heaters pre-heat when power is cheap or clean and coast through peaks, making the humble tank the cheapest grid storage available (~$100/kWh-equivalent) via the CTA-2045/EcoPort standard.

companies.name: Rheem
companies.what: ENERGY STAR connected water heaters with built-in EcoPort (CTA-2045) ports and EcoNet platform for utility load-shifting programs.
companies.signal: One of the two dominant US water-heater OEMs; CTA-2045 now mandated on electric tanks in WA/OR

companies.name: A. O. Smith
companies.what: Connected heat-pump water heaters with CTA-2045 modules validated in utility load-shifting studies (up to ~78% of energy shed-shifted).
companies.signal: Major OEM in ENERGY STAR connected water heater programs

companies.name: Shifted Energy
companies.what: Retrofits and aggregates fleets of (often multifamily) electric water heaters for second-by-second grid balancing.
companies.signal: Fleet has provided fast frequency response in Hawaiian Electric's Power Partnerships program for over a year

companies.name: Steffes
companies.what: Grid-enabled water heating controls and ETS systems long deployed by rural co-ops and municipal utilities for load management.
companies.signal: Decades-long incumbent in utility-controlled water heating

companies.name: Mixergy
companies.what: UK smart stratified hot-water cylinders that heat only the water needed and respond to tariff/grid signals.
companies.signal: Tens of thousands of UK installs via housing providers and energy suppliers

variations.white_space: Despite being the cheapest flexible storage on the grid, this space has almost no venture activity: water heaters are sold through plumbers on burnout replacement, and the flexibility value accrues to utilities rather than the homeowner (split incentives). State CTA-2045 mandates (WA, OR) and 15-minute wholesale settlement create an opening for fleet aggregators and OEM-embedded software, as consumer retrofit plays (e.g., Aquanta) never reached scale.

variations.name: Smart ventilation, HRV/ERV and IAQ-driven HVAC load reduction
variations.description: Demand-controlled and heat-recovery ventilation plus sorbent air cleaning deliver required fresh air with far less conditioning energy — attacking the ventilation share of HVAC load while improving indoor air quality.

companies.name: Zehnder
companies.what: European leader in high-efficiency HRV/ERV (ComfoAir) recovering up to ~90% of heat from exhaust air in tight, electrified homes.
companies.signal: Listed Swiss group; the default ventilation spec for Passive House projects

companies.name: enVerid
companies.what: Sorbent-based HVAC Load Reduction modules that scrub CO2/VOCs indoors so buildings can cut outside-air intake up to 80% and HVAC energy up to 40% under ASHRAE 62.1 IAQP.
companies.signal: $20M round (2020) plus DOE cost-shared development; effectively alone in sorbent OA-reduction

companies.name: Airthings
companies.what: Radon/CO2/IAQ sensors whose 'Airthings for Business' data drives demand-controlled ventilation and HVAC optimization.
companies.signal: Oslo Bors-listed; millions of sensors sold

companies.name: Kaiterra
companies.what: Commercial IAQ monitoring integrated with BMS to balance ventilation energy against air-quality targets (RESET/WELL compliance).
companies.signal: Enterprise IAQ deployments across global CRE

companies.name: Broan-NuTone
companies.what: Largest North American residential ventilation maker; Overture system links IAQ sensors to fresh-air appliances for automated ventilation.
companies.signal: Madison Air portfolio company with dominant retrofit channel

companies.name: Panasonic
companies.what: WhisperGreen/ERV lines plus IAQ sensing bring spot and balanced ventilation with efficiency controls to mainstream homebuilding.
companies.signal: Global appliance incumbent in residential IAQ/ventilation

companies.name: Aldes
companies.what: French ventilation group behind demand-controlled ventilation (humidity-sensitive extract) standard in EU dwellings.
companies.signal: Decades-deployed DCV incumbent across Europe

companies.name: Minotair
companies.what: Canadian heat-pump ventilator combining HRV, dehumidification and supplemental heating/cooling in one cold-climate unit.
companies.signal: Niche but shipping product in North American cold climates

variations.white_space: Ventilation energy is governed by code minimums rather than economics, so few startups can monetize savings — enVerid is nearly alone in load-reduction hardware and most innovation sits inside European incumbents. Post-COVID IAQ expectations plus electrification (ventilation loads on heat pumps) create an opening for controls that co-optimize air quality and energy, and for US adoption of EU-style demand-controlled ventilation.

variations.name: Lighting and plug-load controls (networked LED, occupancy-driven)
variations.description: Networked luminaire-level controls, occupancy/daylight sensing and smart plug-load management squeeze the remaining 30-60% savings beyond the LED conversion and add a sensor backbone for building optimization.

companies.name: Lutron
companies.what: Private lighting-controls leader spanning residential (Caseta/RadioRA) to commercial wireless systems (Vive, Athena).
companies.signal: Dominant specification share in US lighting control

companies.name: Signify
companies.what: World's largest lighting maker; Interact connected-lighting platform turns LED networks into IoT sensing/energy systems.
companies.signal: Euronext-listed; millions of connected light points on Interact

companies.name: Acuity Brands
companies.what: nLight networked lighting controls plus Distech Controls building automation make it the most controls-integrated US luminaire maker.
companies.signal: NYSE-listed; nLight embedded across its fixture portfolio

companies.name: Legrand
companies.what: Wattstopper occupancy/daylight controls and plug-load management meeting Title 24-style code requirements.
companies.signal: Global electrical incumbent; code-driven controls volume

companies.name: Enlighted
companies.what: Luminaire-level sensor network using lighting as a data backbone for occupancy analytics and HVAC optimization.
companies.signal: Acquired by Siemens (2018); now part of Siemens' smart-buildings stack

companies.name: Casambi
companies.what: Finnish Bluetooth-mesh lighting control ecosystem embedded by hundreds of fixture/driver OEMs as a wireless retrofit standard.
companies.signal: Fast-growing OEM ecosystem across Europe/US

companies.name: Sapient Industries
companies.what: AI plug-load management that learns device behavior at the outlet and automatically de-energizes idle equipment.
companies.signal: ~$24.9M raised (incl. $20M round, 2021); one of few pure plug-load players

variations.white_space: Post-LED, lighting-control value consolidated into incumbent ecosystems (Enlighted into Siemens, Digital Lumens into OSRAM), leaving little room for fixture-side startups. The genuine gap is plug loads — now approaching a third of commercial building electricity and largely uncontrolled — where Sapient is among the only venture-backed players.
